title: "Personal breadth" proxy across watchlist/portfolio tickers
description: A cheap, no-new-data-source alternative to full market-breadth indicators (NH-NL, Advance/Decline, % stocks above 50-day MA -- all of which need a broad ticker universe this app doesn't have). Elder's own justification applies regardless of scale: general market trends drive as much as half of any individual stock's movement, so knowing 'how bullish is the user's own tracked universe right now' is useful context even without a real index. Compute, across the user's current watchlist + portfolio tickers: the count/percentage currently showing BULLISH vs. BEARISH vs. NEUTRAL Tide, refreshed whenever the underlying tickers' analyses are. Cheap because every one of these tickers is already fetched/analyzed for other reasons -- no new provider calls.

checklist.step: Implement the aggregate computation (count/% BULLISH/BEARISH/NEUTRAL Tide across the user's watchlist+portfolio tickers) as a new small endpoint or field.
Decide the refresh/caching behavior -- should this be computed fresh on every request (cheap, since it just aggregates already-computed per-ticker analyses) or cached -- and record.
Unit tests covering an empty watchlist, an all-bullish watchlist, and a mixed one.
Regenerate backend/openapi.json/frontend types; document as an explicit approximation of true market breadth in docs/Analyse.md, citing the practical-obstacle rationale from docs/ideas.md.

decisions.decision: New, small dedicated endpoint GET /api/watchlist/breadth (in app/api/routers/watchlist.py, alongside the existing GET/POST/DELETE /api/watchlist routes), returning a BreadthResponse (tracked_ticker_count, bullish_count/bearish_count/neutral_count, unavailable_count, bullish_pct/bearish_pct/neutral_pct) -- not a field bolted onto the existing GET /api/watchlist response.
decisions.rationale: The aggregate spans both the watchlist AND the portfolio (union, deduplicated), per the task description ('across the user's current watchlist + portfolio tickers'), so it isn't a per-item field of the existing watchlist list response, which only ever returns watchlist rows. A separate endpoint also keeps GET /api/watchlist's own shape/cost unchanged for callers that don't need the aggregate. Placed under /api/watchlist/breadth (rather than a new top-level /api/breadth router, or /api/portfolio/breadth) because the consuming frontend task (frontend-breadth-widget) anchors the widget to the watchlist page, and app/api/routers/watchlist.py already imports and re-annotates PositionORM-adjacent signal logic patterns identical to what portfolio.py does -- adding one more small GET route there was simpler than standing up a new router file for a single endpoint.

decisions.decision: Computed fresh on every request; no caching added at the aggregation layer.
decisions.rationale: Matches GET /api/watchlist's and GET /api/portfolio's own existing convention -- neither caches the per-ticker analyse() result, only the underlying raw OHLCV fetch is cached (app.data.cache.CachedDataProvider). The aggregation itself (counting/summing over already-fetched, already-cheap analyse() calls) adds negligible cost on top of what GET /api/watchlist already does per request, so a second caching layer here would be complexity without a real performance need, and would risk showing a stale breadth count after the user edits their watchlist/portfolio or after the underlying OHLCV cache refreshes.

decisions.decision: A tracked ticker whose Tide can't be computed right now (unknown/delisted ticker, insufficient history, or the data provider being unavailable) is excluded from bullish_count/bearish_count/neutral_count and from the percentage denominators, and instead counted in a separate unavailable_count field; tracked_ticker_count still includes it.
decisions.rationale: Mirrors GET /api/watchlist's own null-signal-on-failure convention (nulling the field rather than dropping the row or failing the whole request) -- here, silently excluding an unavailable ticker from tracked_ticker_count entirely would misrepresent the size of the universe being watched, while forcing it into one of the three trend buckets (e.g. defaulting to NEUTRAL) would fabricate a trend reading for a ticker that has none right now. Surfacing it as its own explicit count keeps the response honest about what could and couldn't be computed, at the cost of one extra field callers need to be aware of when computing their own denominator (which is why bullish_pct/bearish_pct/neutral_pct are pre-computed server-side against the correct computable-only denominator, rather than left for the client to derive from tracked_ticker_count and get wrong).

decisions.decision: Reuse the full app.signals.engine.analyse() pipeline per tracked ticker (via a new private _tide_trend helper in watchlist.py, reading only result.screens['tide']['trend']) rather than calling app.signals.triple_screen.evaluate_tide directly against the fetched weekly OHLCV.
decisions.rationale: Consistent with this module's existing 'one place, testable once' principle (already stated in watchlist.py's module docstring for the BUY/SELL/HOLD signal itself): a second, narrower code path that fetches OHLCV and derives Tide on its own could silently drift from what GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis's Tide says for the same ticker (e.g. if evaluate_tide's calling convention/default indicator wiring ever changes). The extra compute cost of running the rest of analyse() (Impulse, Wave, Trigger, confidence scoring) just to read one field back out is negligible per ticker and not a new provider call either way, since the daily+weekly OHLCV fetch analyse() needs is identical to what _compute_signal already does for the same ticker elsewhere in this same request cycle (for a ticker that's also on the watchlist).

comments.summary: Backend suite: 746 passed, 99.92% overall coverage, backend/app/api/routers/watchlist.py at 100% line/branch coverage. ruff/mypy both clean. Frontend suite (unaffected by this backend-only PR): all tests pass, ~99.5%+ coverage, eslint/tsc both clean.

backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts both independently regenerated from the checked-out branch and diffed byte-for-byte against the committed versions -- no drift. New route has response_model, operation_id, summary, and a full docstring; every BreadthResponse field has a Field(description=...).

Verified the dedup logic directly: both POST /api/watchlist and POST /api/portfolio/positions upper() the ticker before storing, so a plain set union (watchlist_tickers | portfolio_tickers) correctly dedups a ticker held in both without any case-mismatch risk. Confirmed by this PR's own test (GOOG on both watchlist and portfolio -> tracked_ticker_count=4, not 5, counted once) and independently reasoned through the storage-side normalization.

Empty watchlist+portfolio is handled gracefully and is genuinely tested: returns 200 with all-zero counts and 0.0 percentages (ternary guard against the computable==0 division), not an error -- matches test_empty_watchlist_and_portfolio_returns_all_zero.

Methodology conformance (verify-elder-signal): _tide_trend reads only result.screens['tide']['trend'] from the existing analyse() pipeline -- confirmed Tide itself still outputs exactly BULLISH|BEARISH|NEUTRAL with no silent default (app/signals/triple_screen.py's evaluate_tide). The aggregate is read-only and purely additive to its own response; it doesn't feed back into any per-ticker signal/confidence computation for any other endpoint. docs/Analyse.md's new section honestly frames this as a proxy/approximation ('not a substitute for the real thing... reflecting only the tickers this particular user happens to be tracking, not the market as a whole'), not overclaiming equivalence to true market breadth.

No new module/dependency/layer added (new route + schema in an existing router file) -- architecture-review not separately invoked as not applicable. No frontend component touched by this PR (only the generated types.ts) -- step 7a placement assessment doesn't apply.

No UI surface in this PR: grepped frontend/src for 'breadth' and found only the generated types.ts referencing the new operation -- no hook/component wires it up yet (that's the separate frontend-breadth-widget task). Browser walkthrough (step 9) and the persisted e2e suite (step 9a) are both explicitly skipped as inapplicable rather than silently omitted.
Decisions cross-check: the one checklist item phrased as 'decide X' (refresh/caching behavior) has a corresponding decisions entry with rationale. No undocumented judgment call found.

code-review skill (medium effort): found no correctness bugs. Non-blocking: _tide_trend (watchlist.py line 71) duplicates _compute_signal's fetch-and-catch logic verbatim instead of delegating to it, risking the two drifting apart later. Also non-blocking: the docstring/decisions claim of 'no new provider calls result either way... already being fetched for this same request's own per-ticker signal computation' overstates the case, since GET /api/watchlist/breadth is its own separate request -- whether the fetch is actually cache-warm depends on whether another endpoint was hit recently within the cache TTL. Both filed to backend-watchlist-breadth-proxy-followups.json.

Own finding, non-blocking: bullish_pct/bearish_pct/neutral_pct are each independently rounded to 1 decimal, so they don't always sum to exactly 100.0 (e.g. a 1/3-1/3-1/3 computable split yields 33.3+33.3+33.3=99.9, exactly reproduced by this PR's own mixed-watchlist test). Not a bug, but worth a doc note or a remainder-based computation so the frontend-breadth-widget task doesn't end up displaying something that looks like a rounding error. Filed to backend-watchlist-breadth-proxy-followups.json.

Own finding, non-blocking and arguable (not clear-cut): the new 'Personal breadth proxy' subsection sits under docs/Analyse.md's '## 7. Portfolio-Level Rules (risk management overlay)' alongside the 2%/6% rules and stop-loss/grading logic, but it isn't itself a risk-management rule -- it's an informational context aggregate closer in kind to Screen 1/Tide (section 2). Reasonable to keep it where it is (it does span the portfolio), but worth reconsidering a top-level section instead. Filed to backend-watchlist-breadth-proxy-followups.json.

review.notes: No blocking findings across tests/coverage (backend 99.92%, frontend ~99.5%+, both suites passing), static analysis (ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc all clean), OpenAPI/frontend-types sync (both independently regenerated and diffed clean), methodology conformance (Tide output unchanged, aggregate is read-only/additive, docs honestly frame this as a proxy not a substitute for real market breadth), dedup logic (verified via consistent upper()-on-write normalization on both the watchlist and portfolio write paths, plus the PR's own GOOG-on-both-lists test), and the empty-watchlist+portfolio edge case (tested and gracefully returns all-zero, not an error). Three non-blocking findings (one from the code-review skill's reuse observation plus a documentation-accuracy nit, one on percentage rounding not always summing to 100.0, one on Analyse.md section placement) filed to backend-watchlist-breadth-proxy-followups.json rather than left only as PR comments.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran backend pytest --cov=app: 746 passed, 99.92% overall coverage, backend/app/api/routers/watchlist.py at 100% line/branch; ruff and mypy both clean. Regenerated backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts from this branch -- git diff on both shows zero drift from the committed versions. Traced the dedup logic myself in the diff (get_watchlist_breadth: `watchlist_tickers | portfolio_tickers` set union) and confirmed both write paths (watchlist.py:216/237, portfolio.py:295) upper() the ticker before storing, so the union is genuinely case-safe; the PR's own GOOG-on-both-lists test (tracked_ticker_count=4, not 5) matches this trace. Grepped app/signals/ and app/portfolio/ (confidence logic actually lives in app/signals/confidence.py, not app/portfolio/confidence.py) plus a repo-wide grep for 'breadth' -- only backend/app/api/schemas.py and backend/app/api/routers/watchlist.py reference it, confirming the endpoint is a read-only aggregate with no feedback into any per-ticker signal/confidence computation.
